verdict.rationale: Runpod documents a REST API v1 that it says provides programmatic access to all compute resources, plus a GraphQL API for Pods, templates and endpoints, an S3-compatible storage API, and Serverless SDKs. A runtime probe confirmed the REST API's OpenAPI spec is served publicly and that endpoints are live and API-key-gated as documented. The 404s at docs-site OpenAPI paths do not contradict this, because the spec lives on rest.runpod.io. missing for 10: independent community or hands-on reports of driving workflows end-to-end through the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Runpod REST API v1 provides programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources. Integrate GPU infrastructure into your applications, workflows, and automation systems.
Use the GraphQL API to manage Pods, templates, and Serverless endpoints through queries and mutations.

https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json serves the REST API's OpenAPI spec keylessly, and a bare GET to https://rest.runpod.io/v1/pods answers HTTP 401 — the Pod-provisioning REST API is live and API-key-gated exactly as documented.
Runpod provides an S3-protocol compatible API for direct access to your network volumes.
